title: Screen-reader heuristics and keyboard model for virtualized tables and live-updating charts
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Audit and remediation plan focused on two hard-to-get-right areas: virtualized data tables (infinite/virtual scrolling) and live-updating visualizations (charts with streaming or polling updates). Goal: produce a set of concrete ARIA patterns, keyboard interaction model, and acceptance tests that work across our component library and satisfy VPAT scenarios used by enterprise customers. This includes: identifying edge cases where screen readers lose context when rows are recycled, designing an announceable row-change model for keyboard users, establishing aria-live strategies for throttled chart updates, and harmonizing token contrast for compact table controls and chart legends. Deliverables: design doc, Figma markup for focus styles, updated component accessibility guidelines, and an automated a11y test harness (Cypress + axe) for the patterns.
acceptance_criteria: Virtualized table preserves logical reading order for screen readers when rows are recycled
Keyboard traversal includes a predictable toolbar -> table -> cell -> row action ordering and preserves focus after pagination/virtual scroll
Charts with frequent updates use an aria-live policy that avoids excessive announcements and provides a single summary for screen-reader users
Contrast tokens for compact controls meet WCAG AA (4.5:1) and are documented in the token registry
VPAT artifact updated with new scenarios and sample markup for virtualized lists and live charts
Automated regression tests added to CI and passing on staging
comments: 2026-02-21 Miguel: Ran exploratory testing with VoiceOver and NVDA against the existing TableV2. Found that when scrolling to load new rows focus stays on the same DOM node but contents change, causing disorientation. Documented with screencast: /recordings/virtualized-focus-change.mov
